text:
### Observed differences

- **Two blocks of activities exchanged their places around a fixed middle.** In the earlier window, A20, A22 and A23 ran early in the trace (mean relative position about 0.40; each in essentially every trace), followed by A25 (about 0.46) and A29 (about 0.65), with A19, A21 and A24 late (about 0.67–0.69; present in about 28–39 in 100 traces). In the later window this is reversed: A19, A21 and A24 run early (about 0.36–0.38) and A20, A22 and A23 late (about 0.64), while A25 (about 0.39) and A29 (about 0.58) kept roughly their places. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS009]

- **Every cross-block activity pair reversed its execution order.** Before, A20/A22/A23 preceded A25 and A29 in about 98–100 in 100 traces; in the later window A25 and A29 precede A20/A22/A23 in about 97–99 in 100. Before, A19/A21/A24 came after the other block and after A25/A29 (the latter first in about 30–38 in 100 traces, the reverse in about 0); in the later window A19/A21/A24 come first in about 27–43 in 100 traces and the old order is essentially gone. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035]

- **Successors switched accordingly.** A19, A21 and A24, which previously led to A30 in about 95–97 in 100 of their outgoing transitions, now lead to A25 in about 97–98 in 100; A20, A22 and A23, which previously led to A25 in about 30–38 in 100, now lead to A30 in about 31–33 in 100; A29 now feeds A20/A22/A23 (about 31–33 in 100 each) where it previously fed A21/A19/A24; A40 now feeds A19/A21/A24 where it previously fed A20/A22/A23. [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012]

- **A02 became a frequent, early step between A14 and A15.** A02 appeared in about 15 in 100 traces before (30 of 200) and about 65 in 100 after (129 of 200), its mean position moving from about 0.53 to about 0.20. A14, present in essentially every trace, led to A15 in about 83 in 100 of its outgoing transitions before and to A02 in about 1 in 100; in the later window it leads to A02 in about 60 in 100 and to A15 in about 37 in 100, and A02's dominant outgoing transition now goes to A15 (about 87 in 100). A02 now co-occurs with A15, A20, A22, A23, A25, A29, A30, A40, A45 and A46 in about 65 in 100 traces (about 15 before) and typically runs before them (about 57–60 in 100, against about 5–13 before; with A15 the order is partly mixed). [OCC001, DIR001, DIR004, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014]

- **A06 and A10 became rare.** A06 fell from about 22 in 100 traces (43 of 200) to about 5 in 100 (10 of 200), and A10 from about 17 in 100 (33 of 200) to about 6 in 100 (12 of 200); their outgoing transitions also redistributed, but the later-window profiles rest on only about 10–24 observations. [OCC002, OCC003, DIR002, DIR003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Chance is an unlikely account of the evidence as a whole: 61 control-flow items qualified where about 0.7 would be expected without a change, and each item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled traces. The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the group A19/A21/A24 and the group A20/A22/A23 have exchanged their places around the unchanged middle A25 → A29, with A40 still feeding the early group and A30 still closing the late one: before, A40 led to A20/A22/A23, which led on to A25, then A29 fed A19/A21/A24, which led to A30; now A40 feeds A19/A21/A24, which lead to A25, and A29 feeds A20/A22/A23, which lead to A30. [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS009]

The placement change is shown directly and consistently: all 21 cross-group activity pairs reversed their order, several at near-complete reversal rates, the successor changes agree with the order reversals, and all six activities are observed in substantial shares in both windows (A20/A22/A23/A25/A29 in nearly all traces; A19/A21/A24 in about 28–44 in 100), so this is a reordering of existing behaviour rather than activities appearing or disappearing. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL032, REL033, REL034, REL035, DIR005, DIR007, DIR010]

Limitations: the earlier-window ordering still appears in about 2–3 in 100 traces for the pairs with A25 and A29, so the evidence cannot rule out that a rare variant following the old order survives; and since A19/A21/A24 occur in a minority of traces, the exchange is established for the traces containing them, not necessarily for every case. Within A20/A22/A23 the internal order remains mixed in both windows, so the hypothesis concerns the groups' placement, not their internal sequencing. [REL022, REL023, REL029, REL030, REL032, REL033, DIR006, DIR008, DIR009, POS002, POS004, POS007]

Other differences: A02 appears to have been inserted as a new frequent early step between A14 and A15 (A14 → A02 → A15), rising from about 15 to about 65 in 100 traces and moving from mid-trace to the front, where it now typically precedes the core activities; and A06 and A10 are now observed in only about 5–6 in 100 traces. The before-profile of A02 rests on 30 traces and those of A06/A10 in the later window on about 10–12 traces, so the exact shape of these changes is uncertain, and the evidence cannot rule out that A02's rise reflects an additional process variant alongside the previous flow rather than a modification of a single main flow. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014]
